questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction the arrow points.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way. Oncoming traffic will stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in bad weather?

options.text: Speed up to reach your destination faster.
Drive closer to the car ahead of you.
Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase the distance between your car and the car in front of you.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway angles toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: An intersection is just ahead.
A construction area is coming up.
You must turn left soon.
The road is getting narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is getting narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the side of the road shows where the road ends. When this line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: How should you treat railroad crossings?

options.text: They are safe to cross because trains rarely come.
They are dangerous.
They are safe places to park your car.
You must always stop at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are dangerous.
questions.explanation: Always treat railroad crossings as dangerous. Watch and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs and signals. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turns allowed.
Right turns are permitted.
Stop before turning right.
Sharp curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash means something is not allowed. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn them to the right.
Turn them to the left.
Keep them straight ahead.
Leave the transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels sharply toward the curb. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: Your accelerator pedal gets stuck while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Press hard on the brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If the accelerator sticks, turn off the engine by using the ignition switch carefully. Do not let the steering wheel lock. Then apply the brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: What best keeps you and others safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn before putting the car in reverse.
Walk around the vehicle to check behind it before getting in.
Check your rearview mirrors.
Turn up the radio to alert people around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the vehicle to check behind it before getting in.
questions.explanation: It is hard to see behind your vehicle. Always walk to the back and check for children and small objects before backing up.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Always drive at the speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Drive closer to the car ahead.
Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, do not make sudden changes in speed or direction. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: You see two solid yellow lines dividing a highway. When can you cross them?

options.text: Only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
To pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.
Never.
Only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction. You can cross them only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. When they are next to each other, only the driver on the broken line side can pass.

questions.question: What are highway signs called that require drivers to follow an instruction?

options.text: Regulatory signs
Warning signs
Information signs
Guide signs

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. Breaking these rules can result in a penalty.

questions.question: What do diagonal stripes sloping down and to the left on a barricade mean?

options.text: Stop.
Turn right.
Turn left.
Go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left.
questions.explanation: Diagonal stripes on a barricade guide you in the right direction. Stripes sloping down and to the left mean turn left. Stripes sloping down and to the right mean turn right.

questions.question: When following a school bus or tank truck, what should you do?

options.text: Pass them on the right.
Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
Stay closer to them.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks must stop at railroad crossings. Be prepared to stop with them, even if you do not see a train.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: Always, no matter your direction.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, no matter your direction.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is behind you or coming toward you.

questions.question: How far away from a fire hydrant must you park?

options.text: At least 10 feet
At least 25 feet
At least 50 feet
At least 100 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 10 feet
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.question: At a stop sign, after you stop, what should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars behind you.
Move when the car in front of you moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then left again to make sure you did not miss anything.

questions.question: When merging onto a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up faster than traffic to get ahead.
Drive slowly to stay safe.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic. Signal, look for an opening, speed up, and merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: When you reach a blocked intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly until traffic moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
Honk to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if you cannot drive all the way through. Wait until traffic ahead clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do?

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
After one train passes, check for another train on the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, check for another train on the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: When there are two railroad tracks next to each other, a second train may be coming on the other track. Wait until you are sure no train is approaching on either track before you cross.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on a paved divided highway if no other speed limit is posted?

options.text: 25 mph.
40 mph.
55 mph.
70 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 70 mph.
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit on a paved divided highway is 70 miles per hour under normal conditions. If a different speed limit is posted, follow that posted limit instead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Side road.
Two-way left turn.
Farm machinery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean you must stop. Come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way. You may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When can you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You may cross a solid yellow line only when you are turning.

questions.question: A traffic light turns from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
Stop immediately.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless stopping is not safe.
Speed up to get through before the red light appears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless stopping is not safe.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow light, slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.
